license.notice:
Lingonberry English meaning corrections, edition 4.0.0.

English and Korean definitions were adjudicated against licensed lexical sources and edited with AI assistance. This is not native-speaker certification. Corrections and new Korean translations adapted from Wiktionary/NIKL retain CC BY-SA 4.0 and per-entry source, history and snapshot references. Original source provenance remains preserved in the immutable earlier packages and correction ledger. Retired concepts do not transfer mastery to replacement entries. No audio or third-party quotations are imported.

Sources credited in this correction edition: Chinese Wiktionary contributors; English Wiktionary contributors; French Wiktionary contributors; Japanese Wiktionary contributors; Korean Wiktionary contributors; National Institute of Korean Language. Wiktionary definition text retains CC BY-SA 4.0; NIKL source text retains CC BY-SA 2.0 KR. Article and contributor-history URLs, source snapshot identifiers and selected senses are retained in each correction record.

Earlier source notices:

Learn Language example expansion, edition 3.0.0.

Original examples and translations by Learn Language contributors, 2026, CC BY 4.0. These are AI-assisted editorial drafts; fluent-speaker review remains pending. Sense, article and grammatical corrections to licensed dictionary entries are CC BY-SA 4.0 adaptations. Stable entry IDs and original source provenance are retained. The authoring and correction records are included in language-packages/sources/examples/. No unreviewed model output, audio or publisher quotations are added.

Earlier edition source notices follow:

Learn Language multilingual dictionaries, edition 2.0.0 (editorial preview).

Korean Learners' Dictionary (한국어기초사전), National Institute of Korean Language (국립국어원): Korean headwords, definitions, translated equivalents/definitions and Korean sentence examples. Original text licence: Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 2.0 Korea. Source: https://krdict.korean.go.kr/ . Copyright policy: https://krdict.korean.go.kr/kor/kboardPolicy/copyRightTermsInfo . Licence: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/2.0/kr/ . Each imported entry retains its source entry and sense identifiers and direct source URL. XML export dated 19 June 2026, redistributed by spellcheck-ko/korean-dict-nikl at commit 42c0d01889f34536e9cf94fe57f62bd2055b1bde.

Adaptations by Learn Language contributors: reorganising bilingual equivalents into study-language headwords, selecting senses, adding editorial levels and topic tags, normalising forms and linking lexical facts. Adaptations are offered under CC BY-SA 4.0, using the later same-elements licence option in section 4(2) of the original Korean licence. Unmodified source text retains its original licence. Native-speaker review is pending; no official exam membership or dictionary-provider endorsement is claimed.

English Wiktionary contributors: grammatical facts and contributor-authored usage examples extracted via Kaikki/Wiktextract. Text licence CC BY-SA 4.0: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/ . Each reused item retains the source article URL and contributor-history URL. Quotation-type examples, attributed quotations, images and audio are excluded. Source translations present in the extract are identified as source English translations, not newly reviewed translations. https://kaikki.org/dictionary/rawdata.html

National Institute of Korean Language, 2017 International Standard Curriculum for the Korean Language (vocabulary spreadsheet revised 2020): headword grade evidence, under Korea Open Government Licence Type 1 (attribution). https://www.korean.go.kr/front/reportData/reportDataView.do?mn_id=207&report_seq=932 . Curriculum grades are not exhaustive TOPIK exam word lists; homograph matches are headword-level evidence only.

The original 1.0.0 starter definitions and bilingual examples remain CC BY 4.0, Learn Language contributors, 2026: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/ . They are preserved with their stable identifiers. App code remains MIT.

Keep source credits, licence links, contributor-history links and modification notices when redistributing. ShareAlike applies to covered adapted content; the app's independently written code has its own licence. Data JSON is provided separately without DRM through the repository download links. Do not apply extra contractual or technical restrictions to the licensed data. No external speech recordings are bundled; speech uses device voices. Store-distribution compliance and language review remain release checks, not completed certifications.

Complete bilingual example coverage has not been achieved. Untranslated native source examples are labelled separately and are excluded from sentence quizzes. No generic repeated topic sentence is counted as a completed usage example.

Wordfreq 3.1.1, Robyn Speer and contributors: frequency estimates used for editorial ordering, not exam membership. Code is Apache-2.0; distributed frequency data is CC BY-SA 4.0. See https://github.com/rspeer/wordfreq for the source-data acknowledgements and https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/ . Frequency is a historic usage estimate and does not establish the difficulty of a specific sense.

Wordfreq source acknowledgements: Google Books Ngrams and Syntactic Ngrams; University of Leeds Centre for Translation Studies Internet Corpus; Wikipedia contributors; ParaCrawl; OPUS/OpenSubtitles 2018 and the OpenSubtitles project; SUBTLEX-US, UK, CH, DE and NL authors including Brysbaert, New, Buchmeier, Conrad, Jacobs, Bölte, Böhl, Cai, Keuleers, van Heuven, Mandera and colleagues. SUBTLEX remains freely available at https://crr.ugent.be/programs-data/subtitle-frequencies . Full upstream citations: https://github.com/rspeer/wordfreq#citations-to-work-that-wordfreq-is-built-on . No underlying subtitle, book or social-media passages are included through wordfreq.


Language exercises: Original Lingonberry exercises and bilingual explanations, 2026. AI-assisted authoring and editorial checks; not native-speaker certification. Reference links document lexical and historical facts only. No publisher exercises, example sentences, definitions, quotations or audio are reproduced. Existing dictionary entries retain their separate licences. This is a focused starter collection, not complete English grammar or exam coverage. Preclude and occlude now have linked dictionary entries; illicit is a contrast item anchored to elicit, not a claim of dictionary coverage. Levels come from linked core entries and are editorial study tiers, not official IELTS vocabulary lists. Licence: MIT. Factual references: https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/include https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/exclude https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/conclude https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/concludo https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/disclose https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/close https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/preclude https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/praecludo https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/occlude https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/occludo https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/elicit https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/illicit

English difficulty review: every stored sense reviewed individually; upper groups use SAT-style/GRE-level editorial criteria, not official exam lists. Added definitions and bilingual examples are original Lingonberry material under MIT. Existing source licences remain unchanged. https://satsuite.collegeboard.org/higher-ed-professionals/sat-validity/content-domains https://www.ets.org/gre/test-takers/general-test/prepare/content/verbal-reasoning.html https://ielts.org/take-a-test/preparation-resources/writing-test-resources https://ielts.org/cdn/ielts-guides/ielts-writing-band-descriptors.pdf

Dictionary practice, edition 4.3.0. Original bilingual contextual exercises: Lingonberry contributors, MIT. Imported lexical metadata: English Wiktionary contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0. Source article URLs accompany the facts; contributor histories are available via each article’s History tab. This release restructures facts for practice and applies explicit reviewed morphology rules. Historical etymologies are not a rule for constructing modern meanings. No publisher exercise bank, quotations or audio are imported.
Original Lingonberry exercises and bilingual explanations, 2026. Dictionary and grammar references verify facts; no publisher exercises, definitions or example sentences are reproduced. Bands follow the linked dictionary entry, not an official exam grammar syllabus. Some phrasal-verb questions practise a simpler paraphrase of the linked advanced word.
Factual references: https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/inspect https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/spectator https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/perspective https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/introspection https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/describe https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/prescribe https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/manuscript https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/transport https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/import https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/support https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/preclude https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/occlude https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/acquiesce https://dictionaryblog.cambridge.org/2024/03/06/avoiding-common-mistakes-with-verb-patterns-2/ https://dictionaryblog.cambridge.org/2018/04/04/i-love-coffee-would-you-like-a-coffee-words-that-can-be-countable-and-uncountable/ https://learnenglish.britishcouncil.org/free-resources/grammar/english-grammar-reference/common-problems-count-uncount-nouns


Lingonberry collocations: Original Lingonberry collocation examples and translations, 2026, MIT. Common lexical combinations are factual material. AI-assisted authoring; fluent-speaker certification remains pending. No dictionary definitions, publisher exercise banks or source example sentences are copied. This is a starter covering every current study-level filter, not full dictionary coverage. Original phrase glosses, examples, translations and answer alternatives are MIT. Collocation meanings describe the phrase's use and may extend beyond an anchor word's currently selected dictionary sense. Study levels follow existing anchor IDs; they do not certify the sentence's exam level.


Lingonberry learner roots and affixes: Original Lingonberry learner-facing family selection and compact English/Korean glosses, licensed under MIT. References verify historical facts; no publisher definitions, examples or etymology prose are reproduced. Origin identifies the historical source of the element, including elements transmitted through other languages and later English formations. These families show historical relationships, not rules for mechanically deriving a word’s current meaning. Dictionary entries retain their existing licences and sense provenance.


Readable English roots and affixes: English Wiktionary contributors and Wikipedia contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0. Source gloss paths, related-word lists and source-reported origins were extracted from fixed snapshots; display labels exclude reconstructed or phonetic forms. Korean translations and editorial transformations by Lingonberry are adaptations distributed under CC BY-SA 4.0, not MIT. Source links and complete snapshot hashes are recorded in the authoring inventory. The inventory covers all defined readable entries in these selected sources, not a universal fixed count of English word families. Some elements have no documented origin or related example in the source.

entries.meaning: On most occasions.

entries.meaning: As a replacement for another thing or action.

entries.meaning: An arrangement to keep a place, room or seat for someone.

entries.meaning: Before a particular event or time.
entries.exampleTranslation: Please let us know in advance.

entries.meaning: To recognise or establish what something is.
entries.exampleTranslation: The survey helped us identify the main problem.

entries.meaning: To help produce a result or give something to a shared effort.
entries.exampleTranslation: Public transport can contribute to cleaner air.

entries.meaning: To keep something in a particular condition or continue it.
entries.exampleTranslation: The school aims to maintain high standards.

entries.meaning: To offer an idea for consideration or indicate a possibility.
entries.exampleTranslation: The results suggest that further research is needed.

entries.meaning: Directly connected with the subject being considered.
entries.exampleTranslation: Include only information relevant to the question.

entries.meaning: Important or large enough to have an effect.
entries.exampleTranslation: There was a significant change in travel habits.

entries.meaning: Slowly, through a series of small changes.
entries.exampleTranslation: The number of users increased gradually.

entries.meaning: Used to introduce a contrasting point.
entries.exampleTranslation: The plan is attractive; however, it may be expensive.

entries.meaning: Facts or information that support a conclusion.
entries.exampleTranslation: There is not enough evidence to support that claim.

entries.meaning: Used to highlight a difference between two things.
entries.exampleTranslation: City rents rose; in contrast, rural rents remained stable.

entries.meaning: To judge the quality, value or importance of something.
entries.exampleTranslation: We need to assess the long-term effects of the policy.

entries.meaning: To give adequate reasons or evidence for a decision or claim.
entries.exampleTranslation: The report does not justify such a large investment.

entries.meaning: To weaken something, often gradually.
entries.exampleTranslation: Inconsistent decisions can undermine public trust.

entries.meaning: To accept or admit that something exists or is true.
entries.exampleTranslation: The author acknowledges the limitations of the study.

entries.meaning: Clear, logical and connected in a consistent way.
entries.exampleTranslation: A coherent argument is easier to follow.

entries.meaning: Possible to do successfully with the available resources.
entries.exampleTranslation: We need a solution that is both fair and feasible.

entries.meaning: Despite the point just mentioned.
entries.exampleTranslation: The evidence is limited; nevertheless, the findings are useful.

entries.meaning: Mainly; to a large extent.
entries.exampleTranslation: The area is predominantly residential.

entries.meaning: A situation in which gaining one benefit requires giving up another.
entries.exampleTranslation: There is a trade-off between speed and precision.

entries.meaning: After considering the different advantages and disadvantages.
entries.exampleTranslation: On balance, the benefits outweigh the costs.

entries.meaning: To limit a statement by adding conditions or exceptions.
entries.exampleTranslation: She qualified her claim by acknowledging the lack of long-term data.

entries.meaning: To support a claim with sufficient evidence.
entries.exampleTranslation: The figures alone do not substantiate the conclusion.

entries.meaning: To make something harmful or unpleasant less severe.
entries.exampleTranslation: Better planning could mitigate some of the risks.

entries.meaning: To make conflicting ideas, needs or accounts compatible.
entries.exampleTranslation: The proposal seeks to reconcile economic and environmental goals.

entries.meaning: Showing careful attention to subtle differences.
entries.exampleTranslation: The issue requires a more nuanced explanation.

entries.meaning: Dependent on particular conditions or circumstances.
entries.exampleTranslation: The agreement is contingent on further consultation.

entries.meaning: As appears to be the case, although the reality may differ.
entries.exampleTranslation: The rule is ostensibly simple, but its application is complex.

entries.meaning: Used to introduce a claim that can reasonably be defended.
entries.exampleTranslation: This is arguably the most practical option.

entries.meaning: To the extent that a particular condition applies.
entries.exampleTranslation: The comparison is useful insofar as the two groups are similar.

entries.meaning: To depend on, be affected by or be governed by a condition.
entries.exampleTranslation: The final timetable will be subject to approval.

entries.meaning: marks the end of a range of time, distance or amount
entries.exampleTranslation: The café is open from nine to five.

editorialCorrection.reason: The range use is a preposition, not an adverb, and does not inherently mean approximately.

entries.meaning: belonging or relating to the speaker; used before a noun

entries.meaning: A pronoun used when the speaker refers to himself/herself and the listener or listeners, or a group of people including the speaker and listener or listeners.

editorialCorrection.reason: Your is an ordinary possessive determiner and is not inherently honorific or restricted to institutions.
